summary: Windy Joe Lookout on Windy Joe Mountain in E.C. Manning Provincial Park: decommissioned fire lookout, now a hikers' hut; BC Parks.

facts.design: Solitary wood-frame fire lookout station with glass-walled observation rooms on two levels
facts.status_note: Decommissioned as a fire lookout; now a welcome hut for hikers and skiers (register text).

access.note: Hiking access in E.C. Manning Provincial Park, administered by BC Parks. A 2004 visit report says the tower was completely open to visitors. No source read describes current access.

visit.trail_note: Hike of about 15 km return (blog) or 9.1 miles round trip (2004 visit report). Trailhead variously given as the Manning Park horse ranch behind Manning Park Lodge (2004 report) or the Pacific Crest Trail trailhead on Gibson Pass Road (blog).

events.note: Canadian Register of Historic Places entry 18052 records a recognition dated December 31, 1941, for the park establishment (Provincial Park (Establishment)); not a date for the lookout itself.
NHLR visit report dated August 1, 2004: tower open to visitors, in good shape, not staffed.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, January 3, 2015.

evidence.supports: Visit report 2004: tower open to visitors and in good shape
evidence.quote: The tower was completely open to visitors and in good shape.

evidence.supports: Trailhead at Manning Park horse ranch behind the lodge
evidence.quote: The trail head stairs at the Manning Park horse ranch behind the Manning Park Lodge.
Round trip is a difficult 9.1 miles steep.

evidence.supports: Solitary wood-frame fire lookout station at the peak of Windy Joe Mountain in E.C. Manning Provincial Park, southwestern BC
evidence.quote: Windy Joe Lookout is a solitary wood frame fire lookout station located in a subalpine clearing at the peak of Windy Joe Mountain in E.C. Manning Provincial Park in southwestern British Columbia

evidence.supports: Glass-walled observation rooms on two levels, integral to function as a lookout
evidence.quote: its glass-walled observation rooms situated on two levels, which were integral to the original function of the building as a lookout.

evidence.supports: Fire-watching work of BC Forest Service in the Cascade Range; limiting spread of fires
evidence.quote: the fire-watching function of the BC Forest Service in the Cascade Range, part of its mandate to manage the forests of the wilderness by limiting the spread of natural and man-made fires

evidence.supports: Trees cleared mid-20th century for views from observation rooms
evidence.quote: trees cleared in the mid-20th century in order to afford clear views of the surrounding mountain slopes from the observation rooms

evidence.supports: Name honours Joseph Hilton, park ranger and trapping rights
evidence.quote: Joseph Hilton, one of the park's first Park Rangers, who held and passed along the trapping rights for an area that includes E. C. Manning Provincial Park.

evidence.supports: Once an interpretive site and functioning lookout; now a welcome hut
evidence.quote: making it at one time an interpretive site for the public as well as a functioning lookout, and now a welcome hut for hikers and skiers.

evidence.supports: Park establishment recognition date on Canadian register
Blog dates the building to the 1950s
evidence.quote: This one was built back in the 1950s

evidence.supports: Hike starts at Pacific Crest Trail trailhead on Gibson Pass Road
evidence.quote: starts by the side of the road at the trail head for the Pacific Crest Trail on Gibson Pass Road

corrections.proposed: remove until a source gives a build year
corrections.why: No source read gives 1925. The register text gives no build date, and the one source with a date (a hiking blog) says the 1950s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's record gives 1925, but no source read supports it. A hiking blog says the 1950s. The register gives no build date. The story reports the blog's decade and does not give a year.

The 2004 visit report places the trailhead at the Manning Park horse ranch and gives 9.1 miles round trip. The hiking blog starts at the Pacific Crest Trail trailhead on Gibson Pass Road and gives 15 km. The story reports both.

sources.title: Windy Joe Lookout, Canadian Register of Historic Places entry 18052
Windy Joe Mountain, Manning Park hikes

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved: the brief says 1925 with no source read; the blog says the 1950s; the register gives none. The story gives no year. Current condition and access are not described by any source newer than the 2004 visit report; the blog is undated in the page text read. The primary register page (historicplaces.ca id 18052) returned only a title in the cache, so the Heritage Guide copy of the register text was used, which states it reproduces the register word for word. Heritage Guide's photo credit is BC Parks, 2010; no photo was added. Status 'standing' comes from the brief and the register's description of a building; the register calls it decommissioned. Websearch budget was used up before a build-date source was found.
